026/**
027 * The configuration of a RainbowGum. In some other logging implementations this is called
028 * "context".
029 */
030public sealed interface LogConfig extends LogProperty.PropertySupport {
031
032        /**
033         * String key value properties.
034         * @return properties.
035         */
036        @Override
037        public LogProperties properties();
038
039        /**
040         * Level resolver for resolving levels from logger names.
041         * @return level resolver.
042         */
043        public LevelConfig levelResolver();
044
045        /**
046         * Output provider that uses URI to find output.
047         * @return output provider.
048         */
049        public LogOutputRegistry outputRegistry();
050
051        /**
052         * Provides encoders by URI scheme.
053         * @return encoder registry.
054         */
055        public LogEncoderRegistry encoderRegistry();
056
057        /**
058         * Provides publishers by URI scheme.
059         * @return changePublisher registry.
060         */
061        public LogPublisherRegistry publisherRegistry();
062
063        /**
064         * Creates a builder for making LogConfig.
065         * @return builder.
066         */
067        public static Builder builder() {
068                return new Builder();
069        }
070
071        /**
072         * An event changePublisher to publish configuration changes.
073         * @return changePublisher.
074         */
075        public ChangePublisher changePublisher();
076
077        /**
078         * Service registry are custom services needed by plugins particularly during the
079         * initialization process.
080         * @return registry.
081         */
082        public ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry();
083
084        /**
085         * Alerts about problems with the logging system itself (as opposed to application
086         * logging routed through the {@link LogRouter}).
087         * @return alerts.
088         */
089        public LogAlerts alerts();
090
091        /**
092         * Metrics about the logging system itself (as opposed to application logging routed
093         * through the {@link LogRouter}).
094         * @return metrics.
095         */
096        public LogMetrics metrics();
097
098        /**
099         * Accounts for every logger name a facade implementation has vended.
100         * @return logger registry.
101         */
102        public LoggerRegistry loggerRegistry();
103
104        /**
105         * Accounts for logger names, and which {@link LoggerAPI} vended them, registered via
106         * {@link #registerLoggerName(LoggerAPI, String)}, deliberately without exposing the
107         * accumulated names/APIs themselves: the one supported way to see them is
108         * {@link LogReporter.Section#LOGGERS}/{@link LogReporter.Section#FACADES}.
109         */
110        interface LoggerRegistry {
111
112                /**
113                 * Registers that a logger with this name exists. Idempotent: registering the same
114                 * name more than once has no additional effect. The first time a given name is
115                 * registered this also increments {@link LogMetrics#LOGGER_NAMES_METRIC} on
116                 * {@link LogConfig#metrics()}, so the running total is cheap to observe (e.g. to
117                 * catch unbounded logger name usage) without ever having to size the accumulated
118                 * names themselves.
119                 * @param api which facade this name came through.
120                 * @param loggerName logger name.
121                 */
122                void registerLoggerName(LoggerAPI api, String loggerName);
123
124        }
125
126        /**
127         * Mixin for config support.
128         */
129        interface ConfigSupport extends LogProperty.PropertySupport {
130
131                /**
132                 * Provides config.
133                 * @return config.
134                 */
135                public LogConfig config();
136
137                @Override
138                default LogProperties properties() {
139                        return config().properties();
140                }
141
142        }
143
144        /**
145         * Config Change Publisher. By default this is enabled with
146         * {@value LogProperties#GLOBAL_CHANGE_PROPERTY} set to <code>true</code>, which then
147         * gates two independent, per-logger-name properties:
148         * {@value LogProperties#CHANGE_PREFIX} + {@value LogProperties#SEP} + logger name,
149         * set to a list of {@link ChangeType} or <code>true</code>/<code>false</code> to
150         * enable or disable all changes, and {@value LogProperties#CALLER_PREFIX} +
151         * {@value LogProperties#SEP} + logger name, set to a {@link CallerType} (or
152         * <code>true</code>/<code>false</code>) to control caller info. The two are resolved
153         * independently - one does not imply or override the other, even for overlapping
154         * logger name prefixes.
155         */
156        interface ChangePublisher {
157
158                /**
159                 * Subscribe to changes.
160                 * @param consumer consumer.
161                 */
162                public void subscribe(Consumer<? super LogConfig> consumer);
163
164                /**
165                 * Publish that there has been changes.
166                 */
167                public void publish();
168
169                /**
170                 * Test to see if <strong>any</strong> changes are enabled for a logger - either
171                 * {@link #allowedChanges(String)} is non-empty or {@link #callerType(String)} is
172                 * not {@link CallerType#NONE}.
173                 * @param loggerName logger name.
174                 * @return true if enabled.
175                 */
176                public boolean isEnabled(String loggerName);
177
178                /**
179                 * Returns what the logger is allowed to change.
180                 * @param loggerName logger name.
181                 * @return which things are allowed to change in the logger
182                 */
183                public Set<ChangeType> allowedChanges(String loggerName);
184
185                /**
186                 * The caller info strategy for a logger, resolved from
187                 * {@value LogProperties#CALLER_PREFIX}, independently of
188                 * {@link #allowedChanges(String)} /{@value LogProperties#CHANGE_PREFIX}. Unlike
189                 * {@link ChangeType#LEVEL}, which is genuinely re-evaluated on every
190                 * {@link #publish()}, this is resolved once when a logger is first created and
191                 * never revisited afterward - it reflects a static per-logger capability, not
192                 * something that changes at runtime.
193                 * @param loggerName logger name.
194                 * @return caller type, {@link CallerType#NONE} if not configured.
195                 */
196                public CallerType callerType(String loggerName);
197
198                /**
199                 * Whether caller info should be computed for a logger at all, regardless of which
200                 * non-{@link CallerType#NONE} strategy.
201                 * @param loggerName logger name.
202                 * @return true if caller info is enabled for this logger.
203                 */
204                default boolean callerInfoEnabled(String loggerName) {
205                        return callerType(loggerName) != CallerType.NONE;
206                }
207
208                /**
209                 * Changing type options.
210                 */
211                public enum ChangeType {
212
213                        /**
214                         * No changes are allowed. Synonymous with <code>false</code> - never actually
215                         * present in a {@link #allowedChanges(String)} result (that case is just the
216                         * empty set); this exists so a single malformed-vs-explicitly-off token can
217                         * be told apart while parsing, and so <code>false</code> is a real,
218                         * documented enum member rather than only a magic string.
219                         */
220                        NONE,
221                        /**
222                         * The logger is allowed to change levels.
223                         */
224                        LEVEL;
225
226                        static Set<ChangeType> parse(List<String> value) {
227                                if (value.isEmpty()) {
228                                        return Set.of();
229                                }
230                                var s = EnumSet.noneOf(ChangeType.class);
231                                for (var v : value) {
232                                        if (v.equalsIgnoreCase("true")) {
233                                                return EnumSet.complementOf(EnumSet.of(ChangeType.NONE));
234                                        }
235                                        var ct = ChangeType.parse(v);
236                                        if (ct == NONE) {
237                                                return EnumSet.noneOf(ChangeType.class);
238                                        }
239                                        s.add(ct);
240                                }
241                                return s;
242                        }
243
244                        static ChangeType parse(String value) {
245                                String v = value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
246                                return switch (v) {
247                                        case "FALSE" -> NONE;
248                                        default -> ChangeType.valueOf(v);
249                                };
250                        }
251
252                }
253
254        }
255
256        /**
257         * Builder for LogConfig.
258         * <p>
259         * <strong>NOTE:</strong> The service loader is not used by default with this builder.
260         * If the automatic discovery of components is desired call
261         * {@link #serviceLoader(ServiceLoader)}.
262         */
263        public static final class Builder extends LevelResolver.AbstractBuilder<Builder> {
264
265                private @Nullable ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry;
266
267                private @Nullable LogProperties logProperties;
268
269                private @Nullable ServiceLoader<RainbowGumServiceProvider> serviceLoader;
270
271                private final List<RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator> configurators = new ArrayList<>();
272
273                private final List<RainbowGumServiceProvider.PropertiesProvider> propertiesProviders = new ArrayList<>();
274
275                /**
276                 * Default constructor
277                 */
278                private Builder() {
279                }
280
281                /**
282                 * Sets log properties
283                 * @param logProperties log properties.
284                 * @return this.
285                 */
286                public Builder properties(LogProperties logProperties) {
287                        this.logProperties = logProperties;
288                        return this;
289                }
290
291                /**
292                 * Sets service registry
293                 * @param serviceRegistry service registry.
294                 * @return this.
295                 */
296                public Builder serviceRegistry(ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry) {
297                        this.serviceRegistry = serviceRegistry;
298                        return this;
299                }
300
301                /**
302                 * Add to configure LogConfig and ServiceRegistry.
303                 * @param configurator will run on build.
304                 * @return this.
305                 */
306                public Builder configurator(RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator configurator) {
307                        configurators.add(configurator);
308                        return this;
309                }
310
311                /**
312                 * Add properties.
313                 * @param propertiesProvider will run on build.
314                 * @return this.
315                 */
316                public Builder propertiesProvider(RainbowGumServiceProvider.PropertiesProvider propertiesProvider) {
317                        propertiesProviders.add(propertiesProvider);
318                        return this;
319                }
320
321                /**
322                 * Sets the service loader to use for loading components that were not set.
323                 * @param serviceLoader loader to use for missing components.
324                 * @return this.
325                 */
326                public Builder serviceLoader(ServiceLoader<RainbowGumServiceProvider> serviceLoader) {
327                        this.serviceLoader = serviceLoader;
328                        return this;
329                }
330
331                /**
332                 * Sets a default service loader to use for loading components that were not set.
333                 * This call will just call the {@link ServiceLoader} without providing a class
334                 * loader.
335                 * @return this.
336                 */
337                public Builder serviceLoader() {
338                        return this.serviceLoader(ServiceLoader.load(RainbowGumServiceProvider.class));
339                }
340
341                /**
342                 * Configures the builder with a function for ergonomics.
343                 * @param consumer passed the builder.
344                 * @return this.
345                 */
346                public Builder with(Consumer<? super Builder> consumer) {
347                        consumer.accept(this);
348                        return this;
349                }
350
351                /**
352                 * Builds LogConfig which will use the {@link ServiceLoader} if set to load
353                 * missing components and if not set will use static defaults.
354                 * @return log config
355                 */
356                public LogConfig build() {
357                        ServiceRegistry serviceRegistry = this.serviceRegistry;
358                        LogProperties logProperties = this.logProperties;
359
360                        var serviceLoader = this.serviceLoader;
361                        var configurators = this.configurators;
362                        if (serviceRegistry == null) {
363                                serviceRegistry = ServiceRegistry.of();
364                        }
365                        if (logProperties == null) {
366                                List<LogProperties> props = new ArrayList<>();
367                                for (var pp : propertiesProviders) {
368                                        props.addAll(pp.provideProperties(serviceRegistry));
369                                }
370                                if (props.isEmpty() && serviceLoader != null) {
371                                        props.addAll(provideProperties(serviceRegistry, serviceLoader));
372                                }
373                                /*
374                                 * LogProperties.of(List, LogProperties)'s fallback argument is only used
375                                 * when the list is empty, so SYSTEM_PROPERTIES has to be a real member of
376                                 * the list itself to always be included, not passed as that fallback:
377                                 * otherwise it silently disappears the moment any PropertiesProvider
378                                 * contributes anything at all (e.g. rainbowgum-micronaut5's own
379                                 * GLOBAL_CHANGE_PROPERTY layer), breaking every -D system property
380                                 * override for such an application with no warning.
381                                 */
382                                props.add(LogProperties.StandardProperties.SYSTEM_PROPERTIES);
383                                logProperties = LogProperties.of(props);
384
385                        }
386                        /*
387                         * Built before DefaultLogConfig itself (rather than left for
388                         * DefaultLogConfig's constructor to create, as before) specifically so
389                         * buildGlobalResolver below can hand LogAlerts to the global level resolver's
390                         * alerting wrapper - the global resolver is built before a full LogConfig
391                         * exists to pull config.alerts() from, so alerts (and metrics, via alerts'
392                         * own listener wiring) are constructed directly here instead. Capacity and
393                         * logging.alerts.unobservedErrorsAction both come from logProperties as
394                         * already resolved above - before any configurator runs, the same as
395                         * everything else built directly in this method - see
396                         * DefaultLogAlerts.of(...) for how the two are validated together.
397                         */
398                        LogAlerts alerts = DefaultLogAlerts.of(logProperties);
399                        LogMetrics metrics = new DefaultLogMetrics();
400                        var levelResolver = this.buildGlobalResolver(logProperties, alerts);
401                        var config = new DefaultLogConfig(serviceRegistry, logProperties, levelResolver, alerts, metrics);
402                        if (serviceLoader != null) {
403                                configurators = new ArrayList<>(configurators);
404                                findProviders(serviceLoader, Configurator.class).forEach(configurators::add);
405                        }
406                        if (!configurators.isEmpty()) {
407                                /*
408                                 * TODO two-pass config: configurators run after config (and therefore the
409                                 * global level resolver above) already exists, so a configurator that
410                                 * contributes additional property sources or otherwise changes what the
411                                 * level resolver should have seen is invisible to it - the resolver was
412                                 * already built from logProperties as it stood before any configurator
413                                 * ran. A more correct design would run configurators first, then rebuild
414                                 * whatever is purely derived from properties (starting with the level
415                                 * resolver) a second time against the now-fully-configured LogConfig. Not
416                                 * done here - see todo.md.
417                                 */
418                                RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator.runConfigurators(configurators.stream(), config);
419                        }
420                        /*
421                         * Deliberately last: alerts already resolved LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction
422                         * at construction above, but only now, once configurators have had their
423                         * chance to record alerts and/or register a real Listener, does "should I
424                         * report/refuse to start" actually mean anything - by construction nothing
425                         * has had a chance to register one before this point.
426                         */
427                        alerts.start(config);
428                        return config;
429                }
430
431                LevelConfig buildGlobalResolver(LogProperties logProperties, LogAlerts alerts) {
432                        LevelConfig levelResolver = LevelConfig
433                                .of(List.of(ConfigLevelResolver.of(logProperties), GroupLevelResolver.of(logProperties)));
434                        var config = buildLevelConfigOrNull();
435                        if (config != null) {
436                                levelResolver = LevelConfig.of(List.<LevelConfig>of(config, levelResolver));
437                        }
438                        return new AlertingLevelConfig(levelResolver, alerts);
439                }
440
441                private static List<LogProperties> provideProperties(ServiceRegistry registry,
442                                ServiceLoader<RainbowGumServiceProvider> loader) {
443                        List<LogProperties> props = findProviders(loader, PropertiesProvider.class)
444                                .flatMap(s -> s.provideProperties(registry).stream())
445                                .toList();
446                        return props;
447                }
448
449                @Override
450                protected Builder self() {
451                        return this;
452                }
453
454        }
455
456}
457
458abstract class AbstractChangePublisher implements ChangePublisher {
459
460        /*
461         * TODO Ideally this would be a concurrent weak hashmap. The reasoning is we may want
462         * a configuration where SLF4J loggers are not stored in concurrent hash map but some
463         * sort of GC friendly cache or not cached at all. If they subscribe to changes the
464         * loggers will never be GCed.
465         *
466         * Consequently the functional Consumer interface might not be the best choice.
467         */
468        private final Collection<Consumer<? super LogConfig>> consumers = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<Consumer<? super LogConfig>>();
469
470        /*
471         * Same shape as LevelResolver.java's CachedLevelResolver: allowedChanges(name) is
472         * only ever called once per never-before-seen logger name (RainbowGumLoggerFactory
473         * caches the resulting Logger forever afterward), so a ConcurrentHashMap here matches
474         * the exact call pattern that made a ConcurrentHashMap the right tradeoff there too.
475         */
476        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, Set<ChangeType>> changesCache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
477
478        /*
479         * Sibling to changesCache, not folded into it - CallerType is resolved from its own
480         * logging.caller.<name> property, independent of logging.change.<name>, so it gets
481         * its own map rather than a combined per-name struct (one map per concern).
482         */
483        private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, CallerType> callerTypeCache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
484
485        protected abstract LogConfig reload();
486
487        protected abstract LogConfig config();
488
489        @Override
490        public void publish() {
491                changesCache.clear();
492                callerTypeCache.clear();
493                LogConfig config = reload();
494                for (var c : consumers) {
495                        c.accept(config);
496                }
497        }
498
499        @Override
500        public void subscribe(Consumer<? super LogConfig> consumer) {
501                consumers.add(consumer);
502        }
503
504        @Override
505        public boolean isEnabled(String loggerName) {
506                return !allowedChanges(loggerName).isEmpty() || callerType(loggerName) != CallerType.NONE;
507        }
508
509        @Override
510        public Set<ChangeType> allowedChanges(String loggerName) {
511                return changesCache.computeIfAbsent(loggerName, n -> {
512                        /*
513                         * findOrNull walks the logger-name hierarchy (closest match wins, see its own
514                         * javadoc) trying each candidate key in turn - per candidate, resolve it as a
515                         * LogProperty and only return null (telling findOrNull to keep walking up)
516                         * when the key is genuinely Missing there. A present-but-malformed value is a
517                         * Result.Error, not a Missing - it must stop the walk right there rather than
518                         * silently falling through to a less specific ancestor's value.
519                         */
520                        LogProperty.Result<Set<ChangeType>> result = config().properties()
521                                .findOrNull(LogProperties.CHANGE_PREFIX, n, (props, fullKey) -> {
522                                        LogProperty.Result<Set<ChangeType>> r = props.forKey(fullKey).ofList().map(ChangeType::parse);
523                                        return r instanceof LogProperty.Result.Missing ? null : r;
524                                });
525                        if (result == null) {
526                                return Set.of();
527                        }
528                        try {
529                                return result.validateNow(ChangePublisher.class);
530                        }
531                        catch (LogProperty.ValidationException e) {
532                                /*
533                                 * A malformed logging.change.<name> value must not be able to break
534                                 * logging itself. ConcurrentHashMap#computeIfAbsent leaves nothing cached
535                                 * when the mapping function throws, so without catching this a bad
536                                 * property would re-parse and re-alert on every single allowedChanges(n)
537                                 * call for this logger name, not just once - same amplification risk
538                                 * CachedLevelResolver guards against for level properties. Fall back to
539                                 * "nothing allowed to change" and alert exactly once per logger name
540                                 * instead, since the fallback value is itself cached above just like a
541                                 * successful parse would be. validateNow's own Missing = failure
542                                 * semantics are moot here - the lambda above never returns a Missing
543                                 * result to it in the first place.
544                                 */
545                                config().alerts().error(ChangePublisher.class, e);
546                                return Set.of();
547                        }
548                });
549        }
550
551        @Override
552        public CallerType callerType(String loggerName) {
553                return callerTypeCache.computeIfAbsent(loggerName, n -> {
554                        LogProperty.Result<CallerType> result = config().properties()
555                                .findOrNull(LogProperties.CALLER_PREFIX, n, (props, fullKey) -> {
556                                        LogProperty.Result<CallerType> r = props.forKey(fullKey).ofString().map(CallerType::parse);
557                                        return r instanceof LogProperty.Result.Missing ? null : r;
558                                });
559                        if (result == null) {
560                                return CallerType.NONE;
561                        }
562                        try {
563                                return result.validateNow(ChangePublisher.class);
564                        }
565                        catch (LogProperty.ValidationException e) {
566                                /*
567                                 * Same reasoning as allowedChanges()'s catch above: a malformed (or
568                                 * pre-split, e.g. the old "caller" token that used to live in
569                                 * logging.change.<name>) logging.caller.<name> value alerts once and
570                                 * falls back to CallerType.NONE, cached, rather than re-parsing and
571                                 * re-alerting on every call.
572                                 */
573                                config().alerts().error(ChangePublisher.class, e);
574                                return CallerType.NONE;
575                        }
576                });
577        }
578
579}
580
581enum IgnoreChangePublisher implements ChangePublisher {
582
583        INSTANT;
584
585        @Override
586        public void subscribe(Consumer<? super LogConfig> consumer) {
587        }
588
589        @Override
590        public void publish() {
591
592        }
593
594        @Override
595        public boolean isEnabled(String loggerName) {
596                return false;
597        }
598
599        @Override
600        public Set<ChangeType> allowedChanges(String loggerName) {
601                return Set.of();
602        }
603
604        @Override
605        public CallerType callerType(String loggerName) {
606                return CallerType.NONE;
607        }
608
609}
610
611final class DefaultLogConfig implements LogConfig {
612
613        private final ServiceRegistry registry;
614
615        private final LogProperties properties;
616
617        private final LevelConfig levelResolver;
618
619        private final ChangePublisher changePublisher;
620
621        private final LogOutputRegistry outputRegistry;
622
623        private final LogEncoderRegistry encoderRegistry;
624
625        private final LogPublisherRegistry publisherRegistry;
626
627        private final LogAlerts alerts;
628
629        private final LogMetrics metrics;
630
631        private final LoggerRegistry loggerRegistry;
632
633        DefaultLogConfig(ServiceRegistry registry, LogProperties properties, LevelConfig levelResolver, LogAlerts alerts,
634                        LogMetrics metrics) {
635                super();
636                this.registry = registry;
637                this.properties = properties;
638                this.levelResolver = levelResolver;
639                this.alerts = alerts;
640                this.metrics = metrics;
641                this.loggerRegistry = new DefaultLoggerRegistry(metrics);
642                boolean changeable = properties.forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_CHANGE_PROPERTY)
643                        .ofBoolean()
644                        .or(false)
645                        .validateNow(DefaultLogConfig.class);
646                this.changePublisher = changeable ? new DefaultChangePublisher() : IgnoreChangePublisher.INSTANT;
647                applyGlobalAppenderReentrantLockProperty(properties);
648                applyGlobalThreadLocalDisabledProperty(properties);
649                applyGlobalOptimizeProperty(properties);
650                this.outputRegistry = DefaultOutputRegistry.of(registry);
651                this.encoderRegistry = DefaultEncoderRegistry.of();
652                this.publisherRegistry = DefaultPublisherRegistry.of();
653                /*
654                 * addInternalListener, not addListener: a passive in-process counter nobody has
655                 * wired an exporter to does not count as "someone is watching" for
656                 * LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction's purposes - see DefaultLogAlerts's own
657                 * comment on hasExternalListener. alerts is always a DefaultLogAlerts; LogAlerts
658                 * is sealed to permit only that one implementation.
659                 */
660                ((DefaultLogAlerts) this.alerts).addInternalListener(event -> this.metrics.errorCounter(event.loggerName(), 1));
661        }
662
663        /*
664         * Deliberately mutates process-wide static state (AbstractLogAppender's field) rather
665         * than per-instance state - LogProperties#GLOBAL_APPENDER_REENTRANT_LOCK_PROPERTY is
666         * a global guarantee by design (see its javadoc), not a per-LogConfig setting.
667         * Last-writer-wins if multiple RainbowGum instances with different values coexist in
668         * one JVM - an accepted tradeoff for a property whose whole point is a process-wide
669         * guarantee independent of any single instance's configuration.
670         */
671        private static void applyGlobalAppenderReentrantLockProperty(LogProperties properties) {
672                AbstractLogAppender.forceReentrantLockAppenders = properties
673                        .forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_APPENDER_REENTRANT_LOCK_PROPERTY)
674                        .ofBoolean()
675                        .or(false)
676                        .validateNow(DefaultLogConfig.class);
677        }
678
679        /*
680         * An enum (TRUE/FALSE) rather than .ofBoolean() deliberately, unlike its sibling just
681         * above - a typo'd value here (e.g. "yse") fails loudly through the existing
682         * Property/Result machinery instead of silently resolving to "not disabled", which is
683         * the wrong failure mode for a property whose whole point is a hard, otherwise
684         * easy-to-silently-miss guarantee.
685         */
686        private enum ThreadLocalDisabled {
687
688                TRUE, FALSE;
689
690                static ThreadLocalDisabled parse(String value) {
691                        return ThreadLocalDisabled.valueOf(value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));
692                }
693
694        }
695
696        /*
697         * Same last-writer-wins/process-wide-guarantee tradeoff as
698         * applyGlobalAppenderReentrantLockProperty just above - see that method's comment.
699         * rainbowgum-slf4j independently reads this same property key at its own SLF4J
700         * provider initialize() touchpoint to decide whether to disable MDC too - see
701         * LogProperties#GLOBAL_THREADLOCAL_DISABLED_PROPERTY's javadoc for why that is two
702         * independent readers rather than one shared flag.
703         */
704        private static void applyGlobalThreadLocalDisabledProperty(LogProperties properties) {
705                AbstractLogAppender.forceNoThreadLocalAppenders = properties
706                        .forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_THREADLOCAL_DISABLED_PROPERTY)
707                        .ofString()
708                        .map(ThreadLocalDisabled::parse)
709                        .or(ThreadLocalDisabled.FALSE)
710                        .validateNow(DefaultLogConfig.class) == ThreadLocalDisabled.TRUE;
711        }
712
713        /*
714         * Same enum-not-boolean reasoning as ThreadLocalDisabled above. Unlike the other two
715         * global properties this one is not a "force/guarantee" downgrade applied after a
716         * type is already resolved - it changes what the *default* resolves to when nothing
717         * more specific (an explicit appenderType(...)/useGetBytes(...) call, or a more
718         * specific property) was set, so it is read into the same kind of process-wide static
719         * flag but consulted at a different point (LogAppender.Builder#build(),
720         * LogEncoder.Builder#build()) - see LogProperties#GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY's javadoc.
721         */
722        private enum GlobalOptimize {
723
724                TRUE, FALSE;
725
726                static GlobalOptimize parse(String value) {
727                        return GlobalOptimize.valueOf(value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));
728                }
729
730        }
731
732        private static void applyGlobalOptimizeProperty(LogProperties properties) {
733                AbstractLogAppender.globalOptimizeEnabled = properties.forKey(LogProperties.GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY)
734                        .ofString()
735                        .map(GlobalOptimize::parse)
736                        .or(GlobalOptimize.FALSE)
737                        .validateNow(DefaultLogConfig.class) == GlobalOptimize.TRUE;
738        }
739

750                        return DefaultLogConfig.this;

752
753        }

807final class DefaultLoggerRegistry implements LogConfig.LoggerRegistry {
808
809        private final Set<String> loggerNames = ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();
810
811        private final Set<LoggerAPI> loggerAPIs = ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();
812
813        private final LogMetrics metrics;
814
815        DefaultLoggerRegistry(LogMetrics metrics) {
816                this.metrics = metrics;
817        }
818
819        @Override
820        public void registerLoggerName(LoggerAPI api, String loggerName) {
821                Objects.requireNonNull(api);
822                loggerAPIs.add(api);
823                if (loggerNames.add(loggerName)) {
824                        metrics.infoCounter(LogMetrics.LOGGER_NAMES_METRIC, 1);
825                }
826        }
827
828        /*
829         * Deliberately not on the LogConfig.LoggerRegistry interface itself (see its
830         * javadoc): DefaultLogReporter downcasts to this package-private type to reach it,
831         * the same pattern DefaultLogConfig's own constructor already uses to reach
832         * DefaultLogAlerts#addInternalListener.
833         */
834        Set<String> loggerNames() {
835                return Set.copyOf(loggerNames);
836        }
837
838        /**
839         * Every {@link LoggerAPI} registered so far via {@link #registerLoggerName}, not just
840         * {@link LoggerAPI.Standard}: an application-provided {@link LoggerAPI} works too.
841         * Same downcast-only visibility as {@link #loggerNames()}.
842         * @return immutable snapshot.
843         */
844        Set<LoggerAPI> loggerAPIs() {
845                return Set.copyOf(loggerAPIs);
846        }
847
848}
